resources.string: Root mode uses a tightly limited UID 0 service and requires Magisk, KernelSU, APatch, or another compatible su manager. Shizuku mode uses the standard ADB/Shizuku service. You can change this later.
NR only can leave the phone without calls, SMS, or data when standalone 5G is unavailable. Use 5G preferred for daily use.
Show VoWiFi Roaming preference in Settings
Show IMS Status in SIM Info
Monitoring is read-only and separate. Choose a SIM below to open every IMS, 5G, LTE+, radio, CarrierConfig, expert, and band control.
VoLTE, VoWiFi, VoNR, NSA/SA architecture, radio mode, IMS restart, CarrierConfig, expert settings, and reset controls.
Easy Mode, LTE carrier aggregation, Auto/Force NSA/Force SA, root-force diagnostics, and selectable LTE/NR bands.

Capture 24 timestamped snapshots over two minutes while you move through a known 5G area. The report records NRARFCN and calculated NR frequency, SS/CSI signal metrics, registration and reject state, live callbacks, PCC/SCC changes, CarrierConfig, Android network gates, and sanitized root radio evidence.
The field-test report could not be created.
The report excludes phone numbers, IMSI, and ICCID. It includes tower cell IDs and radio details, which can reveal approximate location; review it before sharing publicly.
IWLAN is the IMS-over-Wi-Fi transport, not cellular band 1800. This monitor shows Wi-Fi frequency, IMS transport, and the LTE/NR anchor separately.
Serving and nearby cells reported by Android
The modem/Android framework did not expose any cells in this scan.
This enables compatible Android flags and keeps bands automatic. It cannot add IMS entitlement, an IMEI allow-list entry, or tower support.
Profile applied; IMS was restarted. Watch the live IMS transport above.
Android or the modem rejected part of the profile.

Nearby-cell results are the complete set Android exposes to this app, not every transmitter on the air. Tensor modem firmware and carrier policy may hide cells, CA component carriers, or rejected NR candidates.
Enables VoLTE, enhanced LTE/LTE+, automatic bands, LTE+NR allowance, and requests Tensor modem CA for this SIM.
Easy Mode is managing radio settings. Switch it off to unlock advanced controls.
Easy Mode enabled: VoLTE and the Tensor CA node are enabled. LTE+ appears when the carrier schedules aggregation.
Easy Mode enabled. VoLTE and LTE+ configuration are applied; direct CA verification is unavailable on this modem build.
Easy Mode is off. Advanced controls are unlocked; the enabled calling settings are left in place.
The modem or Android rejected part of the Easy Mode request. Advanced controls remain unlocked.
Automatic — modem and carrier band selection
Green always means the modem currently reports signal on that band, including in Automatic mode. Normal color means the band can be selected, but no signal is currently reported.
The modem retained the band selection
The modem rejected this band restriction and remains on Automatic
Enter valid comma-separated positive band numbers
Selecting unsupported bands can remove service. Multiple LTE bands allow CA candidates, but the modem and carrier—not this app—choose the actual aggregation combination.
Common LTE bands: 1, 3, 7, 8, 20, 28, 38, 40, 41. Edit this list for your carrier before applying.
Enabled (the carrier decides when to aggregate)
Bands detected in active radio scan
NSA attachment is available from the serving LTE cell
NR is advertised, but the serving LTE cell does not allow EN-DC/NSA attachment
The serving cell does not currently advertise NR
Modem preference applied; the network can still reject registration
The modem rejected the requested radio mode
Forcing changes the modem preference and allowed radio types. It cannot create EN-DC support or override carrier authentication and network registration.
Local 5G force is active for this SIM
Not exposed by this Android build
All readable Android-side LTE/NR gates are open. The modem will attach when the network offers and accepts NR.
Root force was only partly applied. Rejected: %1$s
The exact pre-force radio masks, band selection, NR modes, and debug properties were restored.
Part of the root-force snapshot could not be restored. Use Restore all and reboot from About.
5G is connected. The network and modem accepted NR.
The LTE anchor advertises EN-DC, so NSA attachment is locally possible.
At least one Android or carrier configuration gate still blocks LTE/NR.
All local gates are open, but the modem exposes no usable NR cell and the LTE anchor reports no EN-DC. Root cannot create a tower signal.
The cell advertises NR, but the modem is not attached. Coverage, SIM provisioning, modem policy, or network rejection may be responsible.
Android is not exposing enough modem state to prove why NR is not attached.

Root Force snapshots the current state, removes band restrictions, enables NSA + SA in CarrierConfig, opens every readable allowed-network reason, enables IMS debug gates, and restarts IMS. It does not write modem NV/EFS. Device-specific NV profiles must match the exact Pixel model and baseband.
The last app action was “%1$s”. That restriction may have removed every usable network. Revert that exact change?
The SIM has no cellular service. IMS cannot register until LTE or NR service returns.
The active carrier configuration reports VoLTE as unavailable.
The current allowed-network mask excludes both LTE and NR, which IMS voice requires on Tensor Pixels.

LTE/NR service and the local VoLTE flag are available, but the carrier has not accepted IMS registration. SIM provisioning, the carrier IMS server, roaming policy, or an IMEI allow-list may be responsible.
Android could not read enough telephony state to identify the failure.

This clears every carrier override, band restriction, forced radio profile, and saved recovery state created by Pixel IMS 5G for all active SIMs, then reboots the phone. It does not factory-reset the phone.
